ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r3.claim: Moses’ prayer shows that he felt the weight of prophetic leadership and asked God for help, unlike worldly leaders who crave status.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r3.anchor: Every word of this supplication shows how heavy Moses (sws) regarded this burden to be

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p25/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p25/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p25/r2.claim: Moses asks God to ease his route and make circumstances conducive to success; divine grace can remove obstacles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p25/r2.anchor: Moses (sws) implores God to ease out the path for him and make the circumstances conducive for his success.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r1.claim: The passage teaches all callers to divine unity, especially the Prophet, to keep trusting God under every condition, using episodes from Moses's life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r1.anchor: Bu âyetlerde, başta Resûl-i Ekrem olmak üzere Allah’ın birliği inancına çağrıda bulunacak bütün tebliğ insanlarına, hangi şartlar altında olursa olsun, Allah’a olan güveni bir an bile yitirmemek gerektiği fikri, Hz. Mûsâ’nın hayatından kesitler verilerek telkin edilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r2.claim: Moses feared failing under the burden of his mission, sought his Lord's grace, and God accepted his requests for an open heart, clarity, ease, eloquence, and Aaron's help.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r2.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ kendisine verilen görevin ağırlığı karşısında başarısız olmaktan endişelenmiş, ama yine rabbinin engin lutfuna sığınmıştı. Allah da ona, bu vazifeyi başarıyla yerine getirebilmesi için gönlünün ferahlatılması, zihninin açılması, işinin kolaylaştırılması, diline açıklık verilmesi ve yakınlarından bir yardımcıyla desteklenmesi hususundaki dileklerinin kabul edildiğini bildirmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r3.claim: God had prepared Moses's access to Pharaoh by raising him in Pharaoh's household; divine favor also saved him from the consequences of killing a man, enabling his mission to free Israel.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r3.anchor: İsrâiloğulları’nın bütün erkek çocuklarının katledildiği bir ortamda Mûsâ’nın bizzat bu kararı alan Firavun’un sarayında büyütülmesi akıl alacak bir şey değildi. Yetişkinlik çağına geldiğinde hata ile adam öldürme olayına karışması da onun hayatına mal olabilirdi; fakat ilâhî lutuf sayesinde bundan da kurtulmuş

SAMIN-DURR:20:26/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:26/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:26/r1.claim: The author distinguishes يسرته لكذا, as in 92:7, from يسرت له كذا, the construction used here.
SAMIN-DURR:20:26/r1.anchor: ويسرت له كذا، ومنه هذه الآية

ASAD-NOTES:20:25/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:25/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:25/r2.claim: Moses asks God to make his task easy.
ASAD-NOTES:20:25/r2.anchor: make my task easy for me

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r3.claim: Ṭā Hā uses أتاها when Moses is sent only to Pharaoh; he then asks for his breast to be opened and his task eased, unlike the broader al-Naml mission.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r3.anchor: قال رب اشرح لِي صَدْرِي * وَيَسِّرْ لي أَمْرِي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except ولي فيها and أخي اشدد, where he uses sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا اثنتين قوله ﴿ ولي فيها مآرب ﴾ وقوله ﴿ أخي اشدد ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses sukūn on ولي فيها and حشرتني أعمى, opening the other listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.anchor: وأسكن أبو عمرو منها اثنتين / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ لم حشرتني أعمى ﴾ وفتح سائرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses sukūn on ولي فيها، ويسر لي أمري، لذكري إن، على عيني إذ, and برأسي إني; he opens the rest.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.anchor: وأسكن ابن كثير منها خمسا / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ و ﴿ لذكري إن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.claim: These readers use sukūn on all listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.anchor: وأسكنها كلها حمزة والكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر

NASHR:v1p224/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p224/r1.claim: Pronounce a moving yāʾ gently and lightly without turning it into hamza; give it its proper length when it is a madd letter, especially before another moving yāʾ.
NASHR:v1p224/r1.anchor: والياء: فليعتن بإخراجها محركة بلطف ويسر خفيفة نحو:

NASHR:v1p224/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p224/r2.claim: When yāʾ is geminated, preserve a single clear articulation instead of stretching it into a soft, chewed sound; excessive constriction is also an error.
NASHR:v1p224/r2.anchor: وإذا أتت مشددة فليتحفظ من لوكها ومطها نحو: إياك، وعتيا، وبتحية فحيوا

NASHR:v1p224/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p224/r3.claim: Direct oral practice reveals the precise articulation, and repeated exercise brings it about.
NASHR:v1p224/r3.anchor: والمشافهة تكشف حقيقة ذلك، والرياضة توصل إليه

QIRAAT-ER:20:26:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:26:3#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:20:26:3#1/r1.claim: The open-yāʾ liya variant contrasts with lī; both are canonical, and liya adds an open vowel before amrī.
QIRAAT-ER:20:26:3#1/r1.anchor: Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Open yāʾ variant (liya vs. lī) — both canonical within the Seven

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p326/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p326/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p326/r2.claim: Knowing Pharaoh’s tyranny, Moses sought ease for a grave mission: acting as God’s vicegerent on earth and facing immense hardships.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p326/r2.anchor: فسأل ربه ورغب في أن يشرح صدره ليحتمل ما يرد عليه من الشدائد التي يضيق لها الصدر، وأن يسهل عليه أمره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r1.claim: The request for ease is tied to the command to go to Pharaoh (20:24): Moses recognizes the immense mission and asks God to make him patient under its trials and to ease it by enabling its means and removing obstacles; the prayer expresses utter dependence on God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r1.anchor: أنه عليه السلام علم من الأمر بالذهاب اليه والتعليل بالعلة المذكورة أنه كلف امرا عظيما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r2.claim: Some connect the request to all of God’s address from “I am your Lord” through this point: Moses seeks an expanded heart to grasp subtle knowledge and revelation, perform worship fully, and endure preaching’s hardships.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r2.anchor: أن هذا القول معلق بما خاطبه الله تعالى به من لدن قوله سبحانه ( انى انا ربك فاخلع نعليك )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r3.claim: Another explanation says Moses faced difficult duties in receiving revelation, serving God, and ordering the lower world; he sought enough strength to manage both worlds, since attending to one can impede the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r3.anchor: احتاج إلى تكاليف شاقة من تلقى الوحى والمواظبة على خدمة الخالق سبحانه وتعالى واصلاح العالم السفلى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī also reads the command to Pharaoh as implying prophetic duties toward God and people; Moses senses all of them and asks for help to fulfill them perfectly, so the request need not be restricted to the earliest divine address.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r4.anchor: أن الأمر بالذهاب إلى فرعون قد انطوى فيه الاشارة إلى منصب الرسالة المستتبع تكاليف لائقة به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r5.speaker: علماء الرسوم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r5.claim: For the formal scholars, “chest” here means the heart, either because it perceives or because it is the means of perception.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#4/r5.anchor: أن الصدر عنه علماء الرسوم يراد منه القلب لأنه المدرك أو مما به الادراك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r1.claim: The added لِي intensifies the request: first the object of opening or easing is left implicit, then صدرى and أمري specify it; without لِي the clause would be complete but less elaborated. The same applies to both requests.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r1.anchor: وفي ذكر كلمة ( لى ) مع انتظام الكلام بدونها تاكيد لطلب الشرح والتيسير بابهام المشروح والميسر اولا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r2.claim: Some say لِي adds a stronger connection, as in “The reckoning of people has drawn near” (21:1); al-Ālūsī replies that this does not conflict with the preceding explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r2.anchor: وقيل : ذكر ( لى ) لزيادة الربط كما في قوله تعالى ( اقترب للناس حسابهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r3.speaker: الانتصاف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r3.claim: Al-Intiṣāf says لِي shows that the benefit of opening the chest returns to Moses, since God is unaffected by whether it exists; al-Ālūsī applies the same point to the request to ease his task.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p182/r3.anchor: وفي الانتصاف أن فائدة ذكرها الدلالة على أن منفعة شرح الصدر راجعة اليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p271/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p271/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p271/r1.claim: Moses asks God to ease the task of delivering the message to Pharaoh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p271/r1.anchor: {ويسر لي أمري} أي: سهل علي ما أمرتني به من تبليغ الرسالة إلى فرعون

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:25-28/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:25-28/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:25-28/r1.claim: Given the great mission, Moses asks for a heart able to bear its burdens, hardship, and revelation, and for God to ease it by creating means and removing obstacles.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:25-28/r1.anchor: لما أمره الله بخطب عظيم وأمر جسيم سأله أن يشرح صدره

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:25-28/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:25-28/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:25-28/r2.claim: The initial li leaves what should be expanded or eased implicit, then naming the breast and matter makes the request emphatic.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:25-28/r2.anchor: وفائدة لي إبهام المشروح والميسر أولا، ثم رفعه بذكر الصدر والأمر تأكيدا ومبالغة.

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r15.speaker: أسماء بنت عميس
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r15.claim: Asma bint Umays says she saw the Prophet at Mount Thabir praying with Moses' request for an expanded breast, ease, clear speech, and Aaron as support so they could worship and remember God abundantly.
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r15.anchor: عن أسماء بنت عميس قال: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بإزاء ثبير وهو يقول: أشرق ثبير أشرق ثبير اللهم إني أسألك بما سألك أخي موسى أن تشرح لي صدري

BURSEVI:v5p291/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p291/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p291/r3.claim: Moses asks God to ease the mission of conveying the message by creating the means and removing obstacles.
BURSEVI:v5p291/r3.anchor: سهل علي أمر التبليغ بإحداث الأسباب ورفع الموانع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r1.speaker: القاضي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r1.claim: Al-Qadi says reciting the differing forms is permissible, provided they are transmitted from the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي في كلامه المتقدم: «فجائز أن يقرأ بهذه الوجوه على اختلافها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r2.claim: Many scholars, including Abu Ubayd, understand the seven letters as seven tribal languages, each contributing part of the Qur'anic language.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r2.anchor: ومال كثير من أهل العلم كأبي عبيد، وغيره، إلى أن معنى الحديث المذكور أنه أنزل على سبع لغات لسبع قبائل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r3.claim: The proposed tribes are first Quraysh, then Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr, where the Prophet was nursed and raised, followed by nearby tribes whose dialects he encountered around Mecca.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r3.anchor: فأصل ذلك وقاعدته قريش، ثم بنو سعد بن بكر، لأن النبي عليه السلام قرشي، واسترضع في بني سعد، ونشأ فيهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r4.claim: The author's list continues with Kinanah, Hudhayl, Thaqif, Khuza'a, Asad, Dabba and their associates, then Tamim, Qays, and related central Arabian tribes; these dialects constitute the seven letters' expressive variations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r4.anchor: ثم ترعرع وعقت تمائمه وهو يخالط في اللسان كنانة، وهذيلا، وثقيفا، وخزاعة، وأسدا، وضبة، وألفافها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r5.speaker: ثابت بن قاسم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r5.claim: Thabit ibn Qasim proposes seven groupings—Quraysh, Kinanah, Asad, Hudhayl, Tamim, Dabba and associates, and Qays—which together encompass the Mudar tribes and their dialects.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r5.anchor: قال ثابت بن قاسم: «لو قلنا من هذه الأحرف لقريش، ومنها لكنانة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r6.claim: The author's account resembles Thabit's; these central Arabian dialects reached eloquence, remained free of foreign influence, and made the Qur'an's inimitability evident.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق: وهذا نحو ما ذكرناه، وهذه الجملة هي التي انتهت إليها الفصاحة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r7.claim: Their linguistic purity arose because they lived in central Arabia—Hijaz, Najd, and Tihama—where foreign peoples had not penetrated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p45#2/r7.anchor: وسبب سلامتها أنها في وسط جزيرة العرب في الحجاز ونجد وتهامة فلم تطرقها الأمم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r1.claim: The Yemeni contribution, contrary to Abu Ubayd and al-Mubarrad's broader inclusion of Yemen, is limited to Yemeni words adopted by Hijaz Arabs; distinctive forms such as الزخيخ and القلوبي do not occur in the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r1.anchor: وذلك عندي إنما هو فيما استعملته عرب الحجاز من لغة اليمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r2.claim: Languages near Iraq were altered by Persian, Nabataean, and Hira Christian contact; northern Syria by Romans and Israelites; western mountain areas remained sparsely inhabited.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r2.anchor: وأما ما والى العراق من جزيرة العرب، وهي بلاد ربيعة، وشرقي الجزيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r3.claim: The intermediate tribes' language remained clear of foreign influence, and later philologists in Basra and Kufa recorded from them while avoiding Yemen, Iraq, and Syria.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r3.anchor: فبقيت القبائل المذكورة سليمة اللغات لم تكدر صفو كلامها أمة من العجم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r4.claim: Mecca, Medina, and Taif were also avoided as linguistic sources because foreign captives and traders had affected their speech; they had remained pure during the Prophet's time when contact was limited.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r4.anchor: وكذلك تجنبوا حواضر الحجاز مكة، والمدينة، والطائف. لأن السبي والتجار من الأمم كثروا فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r5.claim: The seven letters are expressions from seven tribes: the same meaning may be conveyed in Qurayshi, Hudhayli, or another wording according to eloquence and concision; the Qur'anic word فطر was clarified to Ibn Abbas by a Bedouin's claim to have originated a well.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p46/r5.anchor: فمعنى قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف» أي فيه عبارات سبع قبائل بلغة جملتها نزل القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p281#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p281#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p281#3/r1.claim: The request means: make easy for me the task for which You have commissioned me.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p281#3/r1.anchor: ومعنى قوله يسر لي أمري سهل علي ما بعثتني له

JISHUMI:v6p4651/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4651/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4651/r11.claim: Taysīr is making something easy, the opposite of making it difficult.
JISHUMI:v6p4651/r11.anchor: والتيسير تسهيل الأمر، يسره ييسره تيسيرا وهو ميسر، ونقيضه: التعسير

NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#6/r1.claim: Make easy the task commanded of me: delivering the message to Pharaoh.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#6/r1.anchor: وسهل ما أمرتني به من تبليغ الرسالة إلى فرعون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#6/r2.claim: Make my affair easy reinforces expand my chest by repeating its meaning first generally and then specifically; naming chest and affair clarifies what is to be expanded and eased.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#6/r2.anchor: أكد من اشرح صدري لانه تكرير للمعنى الواحد من طريقي الاجمالي والتفصيل

QASHANI:20:25-28/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:25-28/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:25-28/r2.claim: Making the affair easy means enabling the mission's audience to accept God's religion and supplying support against its opponents.
QASHANI:20:25-28/r2.anchor: أي: أمر الدعوة بتوفيقهم لقبول دينك وإمدادي على المعاندين

RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r1.claim: Razi resumes his earlier discussion of the benefits and conditions of supplication under 2:286 and adds points relevant to Moses’ prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r1.anchor: أما البحث الأول : وهو فائدة الدعاء وشرائطه فقد تقدم في تفسير قوله : { ربنا لا تؤاخذنا

RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r2.claim: The highest degree of perfection is to be perfect in oneself and to perfect others; God is eternally perfect in Himself but perfects others in time.
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r2.anchor: للكمال مراتب ودرجات وأعلاها أن يكون كاملا في ذاته مكملا لغيره

RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r3.claim: Although perfecting others is a perfection, its absence from eternity is no defect: perfecting means making something complete, and eternally making the already complete is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r3.anchor: التكميل عبارة عن جعل الشيء كاملا وذلك لا يتحقق إلا عند عدم الكمال

RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r4.claim: The objection that God would lack a perfection if He did not perfect eternally fails because eternal action is impossible; impossibilities such as making a self or counting endless motions do not imply incapacity.
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r4.anchor: النقصان إنما يلزم لو كان ذلك ممكنا في الأزل لكنا بينا أن الفعل الأزلي محال

RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r5.claim: God brings some possibilities into existence because nonexistents are infinite; bringing all into being would mean an infinite number entered existence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r5.anchor: أن المعدومات غير متناهية فلو أجلس الكل على مائدة الوجود لدخل ما لا نهاية له في الوجود

RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r6.claim: If God created all possibilities, He could create nothing afterward, since creating what already exists is impossible and this would turn ability into incapacity.
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r6.anchor: أنه لو أوجد الكل لما بقي بعد ذلك قادرا على الإيجاد لأن إيجاد الموجود محال

RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r7.claim: Creating everything would erase distinctions between the capable agent and what is naturally necessary; capacity is perfection, while natural necessity is deficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r7.anchor: لو دخل الكل في الوجود لما بقي فيه تمييز فلا يتميز القادر على الموجب والقدرة كمال

RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p28/r8.claim: An objection says the finite number of existent things is a small banquet compared with infinitely many deprived nonexistents; selection either presupposes an unexplained entitlement or is purposeless.

RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r1.claim: The objection is framed as God giving and withholding neither from stinginess nor generosity, which would seem unworthy of the Most Generous.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r1.anchor: يعطي ويمنع لا بخلا ولا كرما

RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r2.claim: Razi answers that these doubts project human choices onto God; God is not questioned about what He does, while people are, as 21:23 states.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r2.anchor: أن هذه الشبهات إنما تدور في العقول والخيالات لأن الإنسان يحاول قياس فعله على فعلنا

RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r3.claim: The universal outpouring of existence from divine mercy is the general hospitality and comprehensive table meant by 7:156.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r3.anchor: هذا الوجود الفائض من نور رحمته على جميع الممكنات هو الضيافة العامة والمائدة الشاملة

RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r4.claim: Animals surpass inanimate things because they distinguish existence from nonexistence and use inanimate things as tools, whereas inanimates have no awareness of their own existence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r4.anchor: الجماد لا خبر عنده من وجوده فوجوده بالنسبة إليه كالعدم وعدمه كالوجود

RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r5.claim: Just as mercy gave existence to some possibilities, it gives life to some existent things and leaves others inanimate; life is to inanimacy as light, sight, and existence are to their opposites.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r5.anchor: اقتضيا وضع مائدة الحياة لبعض الموجودات دون البعض

RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r6.claim: Living beings perceive pleasure and pain, good and evil, and therefore need power to pursue what benefits them and flee harm; without it they would remain helpless prey.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r6.anchor: احتجنا إلى طلب الملائم ودفع المنافي فإن لم تكن لنا قدرة على الهرب والطلب والدفع والجذب

RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r7.claim: Complete mercy grants power to some living beings, just as it grants life to some existent things and existence to some nonexistents.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29/r7.anchor: فاقتضت الرحمة التامة تخصيص بعض الأحياء بالقدرة كما اقتضت تخصيص بعض الموجودات بالحياة

RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r1.speaker: الله تعالى
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r1.claim: Razi cites a saying addressed to the intellect: through it God humiliates, rewards, and punishes; he uses this to frame reason as an honored gift, without giving a grading.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r1.anchor: بك أهين وبك أثيب وبك أعاقب

RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r2.claim: God grants reason, insight, and guidance; existence, life, power, and reason are four gifts, with reason completing the set.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r2.anchor: فعند هذه الدرجة فازوا بالخلع الأربعة

RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r3.claim: As the final Prophet is the best of the prophets and humans are the best bodily creatures, reason is best among the gifts because it comes last.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r3.anchor: الخاتم يجب أن يكون أفضل ألا ترى أن رسولنا صلى الله عليه وسلم لما كان خاتم النبيين كان أفضل الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r4.claim: Reason’s innate necessary truths are like shining stars: just as stars guide travelers through earthly darkness, these truths guide minds toward the spiritual world.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r4.anchor: العلوم الضرورية البديهية المركوزة في بدائه العقول

RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r5.claim: Reason sees the mark of createdness on its own knowledge and gifts, inferring an inscriber from the inscriptions and recognizing that maker and building differ from what is made.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r5.anchor: رأى رقم الحدوث على تلك الجواهر وعلى جميع تلك الخلع فاستدل بتلك الأرقام على راقم

RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r8.claim: No act occurs until the servant wills it, but a created will needs an agent; if the servant creates it, another will is needed endlessly, so God creates the will and truly facilitates affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v22p29#2/r8.anchor: فهذه الإرادة صفة محدثة ولا بد لها من فاعل وفاعلها إن كان هو العبد افتقر في تحصيل تلك الإرادة إلى إرادة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r1.claim: Expanding the breast expresses the recipient’s readiness and facilitating the affair expresses the agent’s efficacy; God grants both, so the two prayers argue that all events occur by His decree, wisdom, and power.
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r1.anchor: وعبر عن حصول الفاعل بقوله : { ويسر لى أمرى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r2.claim: One reading is that Moses asks not only for an open breast but also for the actual execution of his mission and attainment of its goal.
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r2.anchor: كأن موسى عليه السلام قال : إلهي لا أكتفي بشرح الصدر ولكن أطلب منك تنفيذ الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r3.claim: Another reading pairs God’s four gifts of existence, life, power, and reason with four services in prayer: standing, recitation, bowing, and prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r3.anchor: وأقم الصلاة لذكري فإن فيها أنواعا أربعة من الخدمة

RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r4.claim: A further reading treats prophethood as a fifth gift and the prophetic mission as its corresponding service; Moses asks for help because of his weakness, limited means, and powerful opponent.
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r4.anchor: لما أعطاه الخلعة الخامسة وهي خلعة الرسالة قال : { رب اشرح لى صدرى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r5.claim: Supplication is a means of nearness to God, and Moses prayed here seeking that nearness; Razi says he will establish that prayer brings closeness and that Moses sought it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r5.anchor: الدعاء سبب القرب من الله تعالى وإنما اشتغل موسى بهذا الدعاء طلبا للقرب

RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r6.claim: Razi points to Qur’anic question-and-answer passages on theological matters: the crescents, the spirit, the mountains, and the Hour.
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r6.anchor: ذكر السؤال والجواب في كتابه في عدة مواضع منها أصولية ومنها فروعية

RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r7.claim: He also notes six successive legal questions in al-Baqara, beginning with what people should spend and the answer naming parents and relatives.
RAZI-FULL:v22p30/r7.anchor: أحدها : { يسئلونك ماذا ينفقون قل ما أنفقتم من خير فللوالدين

RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r3.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r3.claim: The Sunnis explain Moses' request for ease as asking God to create ease in his affair.
RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r3.anchor: والمراد منه عند أهل السنة خلقها وعند المعتزلة تحريك الدواعي والبواعث

RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r4.claim: The Mu'tazilites interpret the request as God activating motives and incentives through facilitative acts of grace.
RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r4.anchor: عند المعتزلة تحريك الدواعي والبواعث بفعل الألطاف المسهلة

RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r5.claim: Although God has already done every grace that could be done, some graces may only properly be given after this request; asking makes their provision fitting.
RAZI-FULL:v22p41/r5.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون هناك من الألطاف ما لا يحسن فعلها إلا بعد هذا السؤال

RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r5.claim: The soul receives unseen forms from the angelic realm through thought, then conveys them to the physical world through speech; thought is a great act of worship, and speech is its noble means of teaching others.
RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r5.anchor: روحه من عالم الملائكة فهو يستفيد أبدا صور المغيبات من عالم الملائكة ثم بعد تلك الاستفادة

RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r6.claim: The requests form a sequence: chest expansion gives spiritual light, ease facilitates acquiring it, and the tongue then conveys that spiritual perfection to others.
RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى طلب النور الواقع في الروح

STUDYQURAN:20:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:25/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:25/r1.claim: Muslims commonly recite this prayer in times of difficulty and anxiety.
STUDYQURAN:20:25/r1.anchor: This part of Moses’ prayer is commonly uttered by Muslims at times of difficulty and anxiety

SULAMI:v1p441/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p441/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p441/r2.claim: Ibn Ata asks to see none but God, act and speak only through knowledge of Him, and loosen the human knot of the tongue so that Moses speaks only what he has received from God.
SULAMI:v1p441/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : اكشف لي عن صدري حتى لا أشاهد غيرك

SULAMI:v1p441/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p441/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p441/r5.claim: Ibn Ata asks God to uncover his heart so he sees none but Him, free him from self-regard, and make him speak only of God's favor and what brings him near.
SULAMI:v1p441/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : اشرح لي صدري ' اكشف لي قلبي

SULAMI:v1p441/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p441/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p441/r7.claim: Ibn Ata reads the requests as opening the breast to hear God, easing the affair through abiding with Him, and loosening the ego's knot from the tongue.
SULAMI:v1p441/r7.anchor: سمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت أبا القاسم البزار يقول : قال ابن عطاء

SULAMI:v1p441/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p441/r8.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p441/r8.claim: Junayd says Moses asked God only for good character traits.
SULAMI:v1p441/r8.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله في قوله

SULAMI:v1p441/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p441/r9.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p441/r9.claim: Al-Husayn reads the requests as progression into direct encounter: expanded capacity for confrontation, an eased course to God by God, and a loosened tongue; once granted, Moses sees only God's part in him and receives all he asked.
SULAMI:v1p441/r9.anchor: وقال الحسين : لما أزال الحق عنه التوقف وجاء إلى الله بالله

TABATABAI:20:25-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:25-32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:25-32/r2.claim: Moses does not ask God to reduce the mission or compromise its demands; he asks that the same difficult and serious task be made easy for him personally.
TABATABAI:20:25-32/r2.anchor: ولم يسأله تعالى أن يخفف في رسالته ويتنزل بعض التنزل عما أمره به أولا فيقنع بما هو دونه

TABATABAI:20:25-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:25-32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:25-32/r3.claim: The phrase لِي in this context implies personal specification: make easy the task entrusted to me, not make the task intrinsically easier.
TABATABAI:20:25-32/r3.anchor: ووجه الدلالة أن قوله { لي } والمقام هذا المقام يفيد الاختصاص

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p388/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p388/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p388/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the prayer as asking God to make easy the task for which Moses was sent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p388/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد سهل علي مابعثتني له)

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r3.claim: God granted Moses’s requests; his speech impediment came from putting a coal in his mouth as a child after he pulled Pharaoh’s beard.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r3.anchor:
ففعل الله تبارك وتعالى ذلك به.
وكانت العقدة التي كانت في لسانه أنه تناول لحية فرعون وهو صغير،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r4.claim: Pharaoh meant to kill Moses, but his wife said the child did not understand and proposed testing him with a date and a coal; he chose the coal, causing the impediment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r4.anchor: فقالت له امرأته: إن هذا صغير لا يعقل، فإن أردت أن تعلم ذلك فادع بتمرة وجمرة فاعرضهما عليه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says Pharaoh called Moses an enemy after Moses took hold of his beard; Pharaoh’s wife proposed the test only to divert punishment from Moses.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257#2/r5.anchor:
عاصم بن حكيم أن مجاهدا قال: لما تناول لحية فرعون، قال فرعون: هذا عدو لي.
وإنما قالت له ذلك ترد عن موسى عقوبته.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r1.speaker: شاعر مجهول
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r1.claim: An unattributed poem depicts an echo in a desolate scene, distant in the dark of night, as an example of deceptive perception.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r1.anchor: وصرماء مذكار كأن دويها ... بعيد جنان الليل مما يخيل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r2.speaker: شاعر مجهول
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r2.claim: A second unattributed verse says humanlike speech, once heard, proves too indistinct to understand clearly.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r2.anchor: حديث أناسي فلما سمعته ... إذا ليس فيه ما أبين فأعقل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r3.speaker: الأخطل
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r3.claim: Al-Akhtal says a yearling fox in the desert looks like an armored horse when it climbs a rise, illustrating small things appearing large.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r3.anchor: وقال الأخطل يذكر فلاة رأى الصغير فيها كبيرا : ترى الثعلب الحولي فيها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r4.speaker: النابغة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r4.claim: Al-Nābigha says a herder carrying a load seems like a bird from his high, protected site, because height alters appearance.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r4.anchor: وقال النابغة : وحلت بيوتي في يفاع ممنع ... تخال به راعي

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r5.speaker: ابن أحمر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r5.claim: Ibn Ahmar describes imagined shapes multiplying and a chameleon seeming to feed by pecking, as evidence of perceptual exaggeration.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r5.anchor: وقال ابن أحمر أيضا في تضاعف الأعداد: وازدادت الأشباح أخيلة ...

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r6.claim: He likens professed belief paired with evasion to someone who pretends to take only morning drink while secretly gulping it down.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r6.anchor: وأخشى أن يكون معتقدا هذا والقائل به، يرفق عن صبوح ،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r7.claim: Belief in resurrection and the Prophet's report entails accepting barzakh torment; belief in divine questioning entails the angels' questioning in the grave.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r7.anchor: وما على من آمن بالبعث من الممات: أن يؤمن بعذاب البرزخ،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r8.claim: One who accepts Satan and jinn exist should also accept possession and their uncanny sounds or forms, as consistent implications of their existence.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r8.anchor: وما على من آمن بإنية الشيطان: أن يؤمن بتخبطه؟

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r9.claim: He rejects calling Arabs universally ignorant or liars: scripture, prophets, earlier revelations, and peoples elsewhere corroborate what is reported.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r9.anchor: وما أخرجه إلى تجهيل العرب قاطبة وتكذيبها: وشاهدها على صدق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r10.claim: The Quran treats jinn as one of two accountable peoples, addresses them, calls them men, and indicates relations with humans.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r10.anchor: قد جعل الله الجن أحد الثقلين، وخاطبهم في الكتاب كما خاطبنا،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r11.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r11.claim: A group of jinn heard the Quran and returned to warn their people; the Quran also describes Satan's touch as causing madness, hence مس.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r11.anchor: وأخبرنا عن طائفة منهم سمعوا القرآن فولوا إلى قومهم منذرين،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r12.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r12.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r12.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites sound reports from the Prophet and early Muslims about the unseen attendant and related beings.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r12.anchor: هذا مع أخبار كثيرة صحاح تؤثر عن الرسول، صلى الله عليه وسلم، وعن السلف

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r13.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r13.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r13.claim: He allows that unusual events may occur in deserts, but says these incidents do not disprove realities people hear and see.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p78/r13.anchor: وما ننكر مع هذا الفلوات قد يعرض فيها ما يذكرون، ولكن

ITQAN:v3p192#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p192#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p192#3/r1.claim: Clarifying after an initial ambiguity can show a meaning in two forms, strengthen it by making it arrive after expectation, or increase the pleasure of knowledge after partial understanding.
ITQAN:v3p192#3/r1.anchor: إذا أردت أن تبهم ثم توضح فإنك تطنب وفائدته إما رؤية المعنى في صورتين مختلفتين الإبهام والإيضاح أو لتمكن المعنى في النفس

ITQAN:v3p192#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p192#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p192#3/r3.claim: The prayer to ease the task reinforces the request because the context is a mission that signals coming hardships.
ITQAN:v3p192#3/r3.anchor: وكذلك ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ والمقام يقتضي التأكيد للإرسال المؤذن بتلقي الشدائد

TABRISI:20:21-28/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:21-28/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:21-28/r17.claim: He asks God to ease the mission of entering the tyrant's presence and calling him to truth.
TABRISI:20:21-28/r17.anchor: سهل علي أداء ما كلفتني من الرسالة والدخول على الطاغي

THALABI:v6p243/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p243/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p243/r4.claim: Moses asks that the task of delivering the message to Pharaoh be made easy for him.
THALABI:v6p243/r4.anchor: ويسر لي أمري وسهل علي ما أمرتني به من تبليغ الرسالة إلى فرعون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r8.claim: Moses asks God to make easy the task of conveying the message.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r8.anchor: وسهل علي ما أمرتني به من تبليغ الرسالة

QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r4.claim: Moses sought the means and preparation needed to convey the message, illustrating that an obligation presupposes ability to perform it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r4.anchor: ويقال لما أمره بالذهاب إلى فرعون سأل الله أهبة النقل وما به يتم تبليغ ما حمل من الرسالة ، ومن ذلك قوله

QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r5.claim: Another account says Moses kept asking because he could hardly stop speaking with God and continued his prayers through the remaining questions.
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r5.anchor: ويقال إن موسى لما أخذ في المخاطبة مع الله كاد لا يسكت من كثرة ما سأله فظل يدعو

QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r6.claim: Moses asks for an expanded breast and eased affair so he can bear hearing another's speech after hearing God's.
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r6.anchor: حتى أطيق أن أسمع كلام غيرك بعدما سمعت منك

NASHR:v2p322/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r8.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p322/r8.claim: The two Medinese and Abu Amr open the yāʾ in لذكري إن, ويسر لي أمري, على عيني, إذ تمشي برأسي, and إني.
NASHR:v2p322/r8.anchor: على عيني إذ تمشي برأسي إني فتح الأربعة

NASHR:v2p164/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p164/r7.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p164/r7.claim: These three open eight yāʾs: اجعل لي آية in Āl ʿImrān and Maryam, ضيفي أليس, both إني أراني forms, يأذن لي أبي, من دوني أولياء, and يسر لي أمري.
NASHR:v2p164/r7.anchor: واتفق نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر على فتح ثمان ياءات وهن اجعل لي آية في آل عمران ومريم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r22.claim: Moses asks God to make his mission easy, clarifying the general request for an expanded heart.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r4.claim: Moses asks God for steadiness, courage, and eloquence, and for circumstances that will help him convey and persuade through proof.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r4.anchor: بل تلقى الأمر وسأل الله الإعانة عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r8.claim: Heart denotes the mind; Moses asks for removal of fear and other barriers to action, then for ease by clearing impediments around the task.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r8.anchor: والقلب : يراد به في كلامهم والعقل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p62/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p62/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p62/r2.claim: The initial general requests are then specified as chest and task; this general-to-particular restatement makes the plea more emphatic than a direct request alone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p62/r2.anchor: قد أبهم الكلام أولا فقيل : اشرح لي ويسر لي ، فعلم أن ثم مشروحا وميسرا

MUQATIL:20:24-29/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:24-29/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:24-29/r5.claim: Moses asks that his task of conveying the message to Pharaoh and his people be made easy rather than difficult.
MUQATIL:20:24-29/r5.anchor: وهو على ما أمرتني به من البلاغ إلى فرعون وقومه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r3.claim: Moses requested aid in delivering the message through an expanded heart, an eased task, and release of his tongue's impediment.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r3.anchor: طلب الإعانة لتبليغ الرسالة. ويقال: إن الله أعلمه بأنه ربط على قلب فرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r5.claim: Easing the task means facilitating the commanded work of conveying the message to Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r5.anchor: أي سهل علي ما أمرتني به من تبليغ الرسالة إلى فرعون.
